standard_code: Class 6, Curiosity Chapter 1: The Wonderful World of Science
standard_text: Science as a way of finding out: curiosity, observing, asking questions, making predictions, testing them through experiments, recording results and drawing conclusions (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 1).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 6 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 1: how scientists find out, observations and questions, predictions, fair tests and scientific instruments. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Science is a way of finding out.
body_html:
How to think about it

Science begins with curiosity. We observe carefully, ask a question, make a sensible guess (a prediction), test it with an experiment, record the results and draw a conclusion. Then we share what we found so that others can check it.

In a fair test we change only one thing and keep everything else the same, so we know what caused the result. Instruments such as a thermometer, a stopwatch and a magnifying glass help us observe and measure.

Example

Two pots of seeds: one in the dark, one in the light. What is changed?

only the light is different

Answer: the amount of light

Example

'The ice melted in 10 minutes' is…

something we noticed

Answer: an observation

Common mistakes

  • Changing two things at once in a test.
  • Mixing up an observation with a guess.
  • Changing the result when it does not match the prediction.

faq.q: What is the difference between an observation and a prediction?
faq.a: An observation is what we notice now; a prediction is a guess about what will happen.
